findings.rule: robustness against hostile input / performance (ReDoS); the previous audit's regex finding is not closed
findings.evidence: _HEADING = r'^(#{1,6})\s+(.*?)\s*#*\s*$' backtracks cubically when a heading contains a whitespace run followed by any character other than '#'. The lazy group is retried at every position and '\s*#*\s*' re-splits the run each time. Measured with evidence_class_errors on '# a' + N spaces + 'x': N=1000 takes 0.92 s, N=2000 takes 7.3 s and N=4000 takes 49.7 s. recorded_release_proofs on implementation.md shows the same timings (0.95, 7.1, 45.8 s). The 4000/16000/64000 run was killed by a 300 s timeout. `livespec validate plan.md` with a 1500-space heading took 4.25 s. This regex runs on every unfenced line of plan.md in `livespec validate <plan.md>` (new rule applied to all plans), in every spec-implement/spec-feature goal render (release_goal_context -> plan_steps) and in the ship gate, and on implementation.md when a release step exists. A single crafted or garbled line of a few KB therefore hangs validate, goal render and /spec-ship for minutes. The same defect class was reported for _CLASS_LINE in round 1 and was fixed only there.
findings.correction: Use a linear pattern, e.g. _HEADING = re.compile(r'^(#{1,6})[ \t]+(.*)$'), then strip the closing hashes in Python: title = re.sub(r'[ \t]+#+[ \t]*$', '', m.group(2)).strip(), or rstrip() then rstrip('#') then rstrip(). Add a regression test that bounds the time for a heading with about 20,000 inner spaces (for example under 0.5 s).

findings.rule: AC-003 / fail-safe: an unrecognised declaration must not silently make a release step local
findings.evidence: These forms are not parsed as a class and not reported by _UNBOUND_CLASS: '**Evidence class: release**' (bold around the whole declaration), '*Evidence class:* release', plain 'Evidence class: release', '**Evidence  class:** release' (double space) and '**Évidence class:** release'. For each, validate returns no error, the step stays local, and require_progression(..., 'ship') returns READY with no proof (probe_ship.py). The blockquote, table and '__' cases from round 1 are now closed.
findings.correction: Flag as unbound any unfenced, non-inline-code line where a case-insensitive r'evidence\s+class\s*:' occurs and _CLASS_LINE did not consume it, whatever its emphasis. Add the whole-bold and plain forms to test_invalid_evidence_classes_are_reported.

findings.rule: robustness: a fictitious release proof satisfies /spec-ship (round-1 placeholder finding, partly closed)
findings.evidence: The prefix list now catches 'pending ...', 'not yet ...', 'TBD ...', 'waiting ...'. These still count as recorded proof and ship returns READY in probe_ship.py: '?', 'TBC', 'will be signed later', '_pending_' (underscore emphasis is kept by _title), '[ ]', 'no proof yet', '🚧', 'blocked', 'not done', 'x', 'false'. The proof cell remains free text: nothing ties it to an artifact.
findings.correction: Require the proof to name something checkable: a path that exists in the repo, a URL, or an identifier pattern (receipt, build number). Otherwise invert the check and accept only cells that do not start with a negative or uncertain token: also strip '_' emphasis before matching, and add '?', 'tbc', 'no', 'blocked', 'not', 'later', '[ ]'. Document the rule in execution-rules.md.

findings.rule: robustness: non-rendered Markdown counts as proof (round-1 fence finding closed for fences only)
findings.evidence:
Fenced blocks are skipped now, but rows inside an HTML comment ('<!--
## Release Evidence
| 1 | x |
-->') and indented code rows ('    | 2 | indented code |') are accepted. Any heading that merely starts with 'release evidence' opens the table, including '## Release Evidence (template)', '#### release evidence template' and '## Release evidence – NOT YET'. Probe: an HTML-commented example table and a '(template)' heading with '| 1 | <receipt path> |' each make ship READY.
findings.correction: Skip HTML comment blocks and 4-space indented lines in _unfenced, and accept only a heading whose plain text is exactly 'Release Evidence'. Placeholders in angle brackets ('<...>') should not count as proof.

findings.rule: robustness: a proof is bound to a step number, not to the step (round-1 renumbering finding, partly closed)
findings.evidence: Labels now come from the step title, so inserting steps no longer shifts the proof to a different ordinal. A proof row still carries only the number. Probe: plan v1 'Step 2 — Notarize (release)' with proof '| 2 | notarized build 1.4 (notary.json) |'. Plan v2 makes 'Step 2 — Device fleet run' the release step and leaves 'Step 3 — Notarize' local. The old notarization proof satisfies the fleet step and ship returns READY. The plan re-review does not read implementation.md, so nothing catches the mismatch.
findings.correction: Store the step title (or a stable slug) in the Release Evidence row ('| Step | Title | Proof |') and require it to match the plan step title, or report a proof row whose title differs as release_evidence_invalid.

findings.rule: error handling at boundaries (round-1 warning, decode part closed)
findings.evidence: errors='replace' closes the UnicodeDecodeError crash. An unreadable implementation.md (chmod 000) with a release step still raises an uncaught PermissionError from _read. `livespec goal render spec-implement` exits 1 with an exception instead of a domain message. The ship gate converts it to 'BLOCKED: [Errno 13] ...' and fails closed.
findings.correction: Catch OSError in release_evidence: list the items as pending with a 'proof unreadable' note in goal context, and raise ProgressionBlocked('release_evidence_unreadable:...') in the gate.

findings.rule: conventions python.md: 'Any is forbidden unless explicitly justified with a comment'
findings.evidence: release_goal_context returns dict[str, Any] without a justifying comment. Release items are plain dict[str, str] instead of a TypedDict. Non-trivial regexes _HEADING, _STEP_HEADING, _NUMBERED_ITEM and _FENCE have no explanatory comment (general.md row 10).
findings.correction: Return dict[str, list[ReleaseItem]] with a ReleaseItem TypedDict (feature, step, evidence, status, proof NotRequired), and add one-line comments to the regexes.

findings.evidence: 'Step 01' and 'Step 02' are distinct labels from '1' and '2', so a plan with 'Step 2 (release)' and 'Step 02' raises no duplicate error. A proof '| 2 |' does not satisfy 'Step 02' (fail-closed). An unnumbered '### Step — B' takes an ordinal label that can collide with a written number; this is reported as a duplicate.
findings.correction: Normalise labels (strip leading zeros per component) in both plan_steps and recorded_release_proofs.
